sections.title: Charged Attack
sections.description:
Consumes a certain amount of Stamina to deal AoE Hydro DMG after a short casting time.

sections.title: Plunging Attack
sections.description: Plunges towards the ground from mid-air, damaging all opponents in her path. Deals AoE Hydro DMG upon impact with the ground.

abilities.name: Moondew Cleanse

abilities.caveat: With a Dendro teammate, every Charged Attack is drawn as Moondew Cleanse, as if Verdant Dew never runs out (in game it holds at most 3). A full Lunar-Bloom team may use it repeatedly; a Hyperbloom or other hybrid team may only get 1–2 in a row.
_curatorNotes: Added 2026-10-16 (⚓ Nate): the PROXY for Verdant Dew. A Dendro teammate is the whole requirement for Lunar-Bloom here (Columbina enables lunarBloom herself), so the gate is teamElementCount dendro >= 1 and every C in such a team takes this form. ⏭ When the party Dew pool is simulated (gcsim player/verdantdew.go: generation stays open 149f after each Lunar-Bloom, +1 Dew per 146f, cap 3; her A4 adds Moonridge Dew in her Q, 1 per Lunar-Bloom, 3 per 18s; Lauma's Hold E and Nefer's Phantasm Performance spend the same pool) only this condition changes.

Frames from gcsim internal/characters/columbina/charge.go (merged main): chargeHitmarkBloom [50, 58, 80] → lands; chargeLBFrames InitAbilSlice(124), ActionAttack 82, ActionCharge 80, Skill/Burst/Dash/Jump/Swap = verdantDewFrame 43. Windup (12 base, 3 after a CA, -5 after a NA) is not part of the canonical FrameMap, as on the Hydro form. C→C is 80 and not gcsim's 89 (next CA not a Cleanse) because under the proxy the next C always is one.

chargeElement dendro, applies false: ChargeAttackBloom's AttackInfo is AttackTagDirectLunarBloom, Element Dendro, and states no Durability (0) — so it applies nothing, where the Hydro form applies 1U Hydro. chargeLandsAfterCancel: the three hits are QueueAttack'd at the press and the Dew is consumed at 43, the earliest cancel, so C > swap still lands all three.

⚠️ Simplification: our hit records call these hits a Charged Attack (abilityType charged); gcsim tags them direct Lunar-Bloom DMG, not AttackTagExtra, so a 'charged-attack hit' proc could differ in game. Hits (N1–N3) copied verbatim from the base form — a sibling form replaces the whole normal ability.

abilities.name: Eternal Tides

_curatorNotes: Gravity Ripple continuous DMG: gcsim skill.go skillTick / skillTickTask, 117-frame interval (1.95s), skillDoT[9]=0.16848 = 16.8% Max HP @T10 (UseHP). First tick 117f after the skill lands (spawn+interval), so firstTickDelay defaults to interval. AoE radius widens 4->6 at Moonsign level >=2 (not modeled).

Gravity Interference (Lunar-Charged variant): gcsim skill.go gravityTick, skillLC[9]=0.084672 = 8.47% Max HP @T10, Electro, UseHP. Fires once when accumulated Gravity reaches its limit (60), which takes ~6s of continuous party Lunar reactions (Gravity accrues 10/s, +34% at C2). Only ONE of the three Gravity Interference variants fires per trigger — the Lunar reaction type that accumulated the most Gravity, decided at runtime. Manual trigger + caveat because reaction cadence is not simulable.

Gravity Interference (Lunar-Bloom variant): gcsim skillLB[9]=0.025344 = 2.53% Max HP @T10 per hit, Dendro, 5 hits (skillHitmarksLB has 5 entries). Only fires if Lunar-Bloom is the dominant accumulated reaction. See the Lunar-Charged variant note for trigger cadence.

Gravity Interference (Lunar-Crystallize variant): gcsim skillLCr[9]=0.158832 = 15.88% Max HP @T10, Geo, UseHP. Only fires if Lunar-Crystallize is the dominant accumulated reaction. See the Lunar-Charged variant note for trigger cadence. C4 adds Max-HP-scaled flat DMG to this hit (see C4 notes).

abilities.caveat: Gravity left over when the Ripple expires carries into the next one; in game a recast after it expires starts from zero.
abilities.description:
Awaken Moonbound Tides, dealing AoE Hydro DMG and summoning **Gravity Ripple**.
Gravity Ripple will follow the active character on the field, while continuously dealing AoE Hydro DMG to surrounding opponents. While Gravity Ripple is on the field, and nearby party members trigger Lunar reactions or inflict Lunar Reaction DMG, Columbina will accrue a special Gravity. Once Gravity is accumulated to its limit, different types of damage will be dealt to enemies based on the type of Lunar Reaction that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina.
Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam: Gravity Ripple inflicts AoE Hydro DMG over a wider area.
_curatorNotes: Frames 2026-07-14 from gcsim skill.go: skillFrames = InitAbilSlice(41); ActionCharge=40, Skill=28, Burst=28, Dash=27, Jump=32, Swap=26. swap=ActionSwap=26; N=InitAbilSlice default 41 (ActionAttack not overridden). CD: SetCDWithDelay(action.ActionSkill, 17*60, 20) -> cooldown 17s, cooldownStartDelay 20. Skill self-DMG skill[9]=0.30096=30.1% Max HP (Hydro, hitmark 21) follows the FrameMap convention, not authored as an effect.
Behavior corrected instant (genshin-db stub had duration:25 on an instant skill — moved to the Gravity Ripple summon which carries the 25s window; Gravity Ripple Duration row confirms 25.0s).

↻ 2026-09-18 (stack-threshold round, docs/stack-threshold-round.md §5): Gravity is a STACK RESOURCE now — three `gainStacks` keys (gravityLunarCharged / gravityLunarBloom / gravityLunarCrystallize), `onReaction source: team` on each Lunar kind, +20 per reaction with `procCooldown: 2` (gcsim: a 2s `gravityKey` status any Lunar reaction refreshes, accruing 10/s while live — "20 per reaction, at most one grant per 2s" reproduces the rate under sparse AND dense streams; an uncapped count reached 60 in three ticks of one EC), `max: 60`, gated `duringSummon` (gcsim gates every Gravity hook on `skillKey` = the Ripple, NOT the Lunar Domain; the kit: "While Gravity Ripple is on the field"). The three Interference hits are `onStack {keys, count: 60, dominant}` — one per Lunar kind, the fire's element is the key holding the most Gravity (ties in key order = gcsim's strict `>` over its index loop) — with `application: []` because gcsim's `gravityTick` attack is `ICDTagNone, Durability: 0`: it applies NOTHING, so the fire is a MARK on the Gravity Ripple lane (⚓ Nate 2026-09-18) and never a gauge application. Divergence stated in the caveat: under a dense stream we fire at the third grant, gcsim at the end of the third 2s window, so up to 2s early. The C1 first-cast tick (`c1OnSkill`, 15s ICD, clearGravity=false) is NOT modelled — it fires with zero Gravity and its branch is the team-composition tie-break, a second mechanism for one visual.

↻ 2026-09-18, same day — THE EXACT MODEL (⚓ Nate: the count was too approximate to be useful). The three grants carry `accrual: {group: "gravity", window: 2}`: `amount` is a RATE (10 per second; `constellationScaling` → 13.4 at C2 = gcsim `10 * (1 + c2GravityRate 0.34)`), any party Lunar reaction opens or refreshes ONE 2s status shared by the three keys, the polls (every 3 frames, 0.5 each) go to the LAST reaction's key, and a Lunar-Charged TICK refreshes it too (gcsim hooks any Lunar-tagged damage; the sim feeds the gauge's `ecTick` events to accrual grants). The fire is predicted and scheduled on the clock at the exact poll the sum crosses 60 — gcsim reaches 60 at poll 119 of a continuous status, 5.95s after it opened, and so do we. `procCooldown: 2` is gone with the approximation it served. The status outlives the Ripple (gcsim gates the HOOKS on skillKey, not the task) — matched. NOT matched: gcsim's `Skill` clears Gravity when cast after the Ripple has expired (`if !StatusIsActive(skillKey) clearGravity()`), so leftover Gravity carries into our next Ripple — the skill caveat names it; and C1's cast-time tick (`c1OnSkill`, 15s ICD, zero Gravity, team-composition branch) — the C1 caveat names it.

The pixel is the blank row; the second sentence only restates the Gravity cadence the skill caveat already establishes, so it is paying for column space twice. Category: expected-but-absent.

↻ CAVEAT RESTORED 2026-09-15 (essential-characters T0; the interim Nate set in essential-characters §6.3 while `docs/stack-threshold-round.md` is open). The removal note below filed it expected-but-absent — the category name-the-pixel KEEPS — and since the Team Builder stopped deriving `manual` effects the same day, the blank is now undisclosed on both surfaces.

↻ 2026-09-18 (stack-threshold round): trigger `onStack` on the Gravity fire — the bar draws from each Interference for 10s, refresh-merged. The `stacks` block (max 3, shared duration) still has no consumer, so the bar reads +5% at every fire; the caveat names that pixel.

✅ THE STACKS STEP (stack-count display round, 2026-09-19 — route A, ⚓ Nate). Lunacy is a stack RESOURCE, `lunacysLure`: one per Gravity Interference (a `gainStacks` on the same `onStack` trigger), max 3, rotation-scoped (a fire lands at a reaction, a tick or a scheduled poll — no segment pool), `lifetime: 10` with `lifetimeRefresh` — the SHARED model gcsim's `a1OGravityTick` states (`CR = 0.05 × min(stacks, 3)` on ONE 10s status every Interference refreshes). The buff is `perStack` and reads the fire's post-grant snapshot (`StackThresholdEvent.stackContext`), so three fires inside 10s draw three bars, +5 / +10 / +15% in the tooltip, each fire a lit edge (⚓ Nate: the value lives in the TOOLTIP, ⛔ not the label). The inert `stacks {maxStacks, durationModel}` block and the one-stack caveat are retired. ⚠️ The grant is authored FIRST so the fire's snapshot is post-gain.

passives.name: Law of the New Moon
passives.description:
When characters within the **Lunar Domain** trigger Lunar reactions, they will gain the following effects respectively: 
· Lunar-Charged: When the Thundercloud performs lightning strike(s) against a valid target, it has a 33% chance to perform an additional lightning strike. 
· Lunar-Bloom: When triggering Lunar-Bloom reactions, the party gains a special **Moonridge Dew**. Up to 3 Moonridge Dews can be gained every 18s. 
· Lunar-Crystallize: When Moondrift Harmony is triggered, every Moondrift has a 33% chance to inflict an extra attack.
_curatorNotes: A4 (Ascension 4): gcsim asc.go a4* — Lunar-Charged +33% extra lightning-strike chance and Lunar-Crystallize +33% extra Moondrift are reaction-mechanic damage multipliers with no schema primitive; Lunar-Bloom generates Moonridge Dew (feeds her Verdant Dew Charged Attack) up to 3 per 18s. All require party Lunar reactions the planner cannot simulate — left as description-only (unmodelable procs).

notModeled.reason: Two of these effects are 33% chances of an extra hit. The Rotation Planner doesn't simulate chance, so the same rotation always draws the same bars for everyone. The third builds Moonridge Dew, a resource the Rotation Planner doesn't track.

passives.name: Lunar Vigil
passives.description:
If one of your party members is incapacitated while in the Nod-Krai or Frost Moon regions, Columbina will revive this character. The amount of HP the character will have upon revival is based on Columbina's Friendship Level. This effect can occur once every 100s. This effect does not trigger in Domains, Trounce Domains, or the Spiral Abyss.
Additionally, Columbina appears to have a special affinity for certain animals who are influenced by kuuvahki...
_curatorNotes: Passive4 'Lunar Vigil' ingested from genshin-db 5.2.12 (capability sweep 2026-07-28). Effect-empty by design: revival HP scales with Friendship Level (account progression — no talent-level-10 value exists), no revive/on-death trigger primitive exists, and the effect is disabled in Domains, Trounce Domains, and the Spiral Abyss (all instanced combat). Not implemented in gcsim (no match in ~/Code/gcsim/internal/characters/columbina/).

↻ CAVEAT REMOVED 2026-08-19 (ruthless pass, Nate-approved): no pixel — Revival has no timeline representation of any kind — there is no death, no HP and no party-state surface anywhere in the planner, so nothing on screen is wrong or missing. It is also disabled in every instanced fight a rotation is planned for, and its magnitude depends on Friendship Level, which the tool has no notion of. Pure kit trivia in a 262px column. Category: invisible-omission.

notModeled.reason: The Rotation Planner doesn't model characters falling in battle, so this revive has nothing to show.

constellations.name: Radiance Over Blossoms and Peaks
constellations.description:
Unleashing her Elemental Skill Eternal Tides will immediately trigger an effect equivalent to the effect of **Gravity Interference**. This effect can be triggered once every 15s.
Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam
When Gravity Interference is triggered, if the Lunar reaction type that has accumulated the most Gravity for Columbina is:
· Lunar-Charged: Your current active character will recover 6 Energy.
· Lunar-Bloom: Your active character's interruption resistance will be increased for 8s.
· Lunar-Crystallize: Summons a Rainsea Shield. The Rainsea Shield's DMG absorption is based on 12% of Columbina's Max HP, and it will absorb Hydro DMG with 250% effectiveness for 8s.

All nearby party members' Lunar Reaction DMG is **elevated** by 1.5%.
_curatorNotes: C1: gcsim cons.go c1OnSkill (E cast -> gravityTick, 15s ICD) and c1OnGravityTick — Lunar-Charged: active +6 energy; Lunar-Crystallize: Rainsea Shield HP=0.12*MaxHP, 8s (shield.ColumbinaC1, self-targeted). Lunar-Bloom interruption-res branch is kit text (gcsim models the LC/LCr branches). All gated on Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam -> teamFaction moonsign min:2. Manual triggers because Gravity Interference cadence is unmodelable. Elevate increment +1.5% (gcsim elevation[1]=0.015).
Prior stub had a spurious C1 damage effect (12% HP hydro) — C1 adds no new damage scaling (it re-triggers the base Gravity Interference); removed.
[A7] Rainsea Shield's 250% Hydro-DMG absorption effectiveness is not modeled; it is shown as a generic 12% Max HP shield.

↻ 2026-08-18: the [A7] line above is WRONG about the fallback — the Rainsea Shield is not shown as a generic shield, it is not shown AT ALL, at any constellation level. All three C1 branches are `trigger: 'manual'`, and `manual` reaches no surface anywhere: `pushShield` (sim/shields.ts:111-115) requires `onCast` with a positive `duration`, and the only `'manual'` mention in src is the type declaration itself (types/ability.ts:649) — no collector, no proc, no chip, no notation token. So the 250% Hydro absorption is a second-order gap on a shield that never draws, and the ability-level `caveat` (which DOES render, gated to C1+) already states the real absence. ⚠️ The constellation-shield wire (53db108) does NOT reach this — it only widened the `onCast` walk to non-ability effect sources; docs/curation/engine-capability-rubric.md P26 names Columbina C1 as one of the five non-ability shields that still draw nothing. ⏭ The blocker is unchanged and is not the shield primitive: Gravity Interference cadence has no primitive, which is why these are `manual` in the first place.

↻ CAVEAT TRIMMED 2026-08-19 (ruthless pass): kept only the on-screen half. Full prior text: "Not modeled: the shield, 6 Energy, and interruption resistance — only one of the three fires per Gravity Interference, chosen by the dominant Lunar reaction."
